images.caption: Figure 2:The CUAWright architecture.Terminal serves as the sole interface between the agent and the task environment. At each step of task execution process, the agent model receives command line output as observation or call a CLI tool to load image into context on demand, and output commands that gets executed. The underlying execution environment contains a runtime, an expandable set of installed CLI tools and applications, and a file system as the agent’s workspace to programmatically manage system state and craft new tools.

Figure 5:Tool-crafted batched visual inspection in Task005. The agent writes and executes a lightweight sheet() utility in the terminal (left), combining 13 JPEG documents into one filename-annotated contact sheet (center). A single multimodal inspection replaces repeated GUI-based image opening and produces a structured response grouping the medical evidence by visit date, diagnosis, expenses, and supporting files (right).

Figure 6:Trace-backed root-cause analysis in WeaveBench. The agent first exports and analyzes the Jaeger traces programmatically, then drives the native UI to verify the causal path visually. The slow-trace waterfall (left) showspayments.gateway.httpoccupying almost the full 4.12-second checkout request. Expanding that leaf span (right) reads back the decisive evidence: HTTP 504, OpenTelemetryERROR, an upstream timeout, andpeer.service=payments-gateway.

Figure 7:Tool-crafted lookup commands reused across a task in Task008. The task (top) asks for a reimbursement claim whose evidence lives in a mail client and a bank account; the screenshot below it is the bank’s transactions tab after the agent’s own search tool has typedCATHAY. The agent writesmail_open_info.pyandvault_search.pyonce (middle) and invokes them 13 times with the arguments shown (bottom), once per supporting e-mail and once per charge.

Figure 8:Tool-crafted click primitive reused across a task in Task070. The task (top) asks for an AWS billing anomaly to be found, fixed, and reported in TeamChat; the console’s cost panel below it already shows the spike. The agent writescdp_click.pyonce (middle) and invokes it 15 more times with the arguments shown (bottom). The trajectory attaches no screenshot; the console view is taken from the GPT-5.6 run of the same task.

Figure 9:BenchCAD heat-sink reconstruction. Reference views appear on the
left, the final render in the center, and an amplified pixel difference on
the right. The submitted STEP file received voxel IoU 1.0000.

Figure 10:Paired traces for tasks 045 and 076. In task 045, Critic feedback
changed the artifact from seven selected frames to a 156-frame recording.
In task 076, three inconclusive Verifier calls exhausted the shared budget
and blocked submission.
